cards.explanation: The answer is to come, buy and eat. The LORD says, "…you without money, come, buy, and eat!" (Isaiah 55:1). Empty pockets, and you're still invited, friends. I've never seen a sale where a bare wallet gets you through the door, but this one is God's.

The answer is False. The LORD asks, "Why spend money on that which is not bread, and your labor on that which does not satisfy?" (Isaiah 55:2). So the labor goes to something that does not satisfy. Hard work poured into something that leaves you empty. I've pressed a lot of cookies, and I'd hate for all that effort to leave nobody full.

The answer is to listen carefully to Him. The LORD says, "Listen carefully to Me, and eat what is good, and your soul will delight in the richest of foods." (Isaiah 55:2). Listening comes first, and the good eating follows. Even I know you hear the oven timer BEFORE you pull the tray, friends.

The answer is David. The LORD says, "…My loving devotion promised to David." (Isaiah 55:3). David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3). That's a promise with a long history behind it, and God is putting it in front of everybody here.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "…nations who do not know you will run to you." (Isaiah 55:5). They don't turn away. They don't know you, and they run to you anyway. That's a lot of cardio for people who have never met.

The answer is True. The verse ends, "For the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, has bestowed glory on you." (Isaiah 55:5). That "For" gives the reason, friends. The glory comes from the LORD, and the nations run because of it.

The answer is the wicked man. The verse says, "Let the wicked man forsake his way and the unrighteous man his thoughts…" (Isaiah 55:7). Then comes the good part: let him return to the LORD. The door is open for the wicked man to turn around and walk back.

The answer is "freely." The verse says, "…for He will freely pardon." (Isaiah 55:7). Freely means no catch and no haggling, friends. When I think of everything I ever got wrong in a kitchen, that word sounds mighty good.

The answer is False. The LORD declares, "…My thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways My ways…" (Isaiah 55:8). His thoughts and ways are not ours. It's a good reminder, friends, that I don't have to figure out everything before I trust Him.

The answer is the heavens above the earth. The LORD says, "…as the heavens are higher than the earth, so My ways are higher than your ways and My thoughts than your thoughts." (Isaiah 55:9). Look up at a night sky and try to reach it. That's how far it is.

The answer is True. The verse says rain and snow "…fall from heaven and do not return without watering the earth…" (Isaiah 55:10). It comes down, and the ground gets watered. Then it makes things bud and sprout, and gives seed to sow and food to eat.

The answer is "empty." The LORD says, "…so My word that proceeds from My mouth will not return to Me empty…" (Isaiah 55:11). Just like the rain, it comes back with the job done, friends. When God sends His word, it doesn't come back with nothing to show.

The answer is that they burst into song. The LORD says, "the mountains and hills will burst into song before you…" (Isaiah 55:12). Mountains, singing. I can't even carry a tune in the shower, and I'm a stamper with a mustache.

The answer is a sign that lasts forever. The verse calls it "…an everlasting sign, never to be destroyed." (Isaiah 55:13). Everlasting means it keeps going, friends. Most things I make get eaten by dinner, so that's a different kind of lasting.
